a:r.a:t: The Reactions in the Urea Cycle

p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting the urea cycle and reactions that feed amino groups into the cycle. This image has two halves, with the top half in a mitochondrial matrix box, and the bottom half being represented as cytosol. Above the mitochondrial matrix box is glutamine (from extrahepatic tissues), where C double bonds up and left to O, bonds down and left to H2N, and right to CH2, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH. CH bonds up to NH3 (plus sign above N), which bonds right to COO-. To the right of this is glutamate. On the top left of this are amino acids, where R bonds right to CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N) and right to COO-. This has an arrow pointing down and right to alpha-keto acid. To the right is alanine (from muscle), where CH3 bonds right to CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign above N) and right to COO-, which also has an arrow pointing down and left to alpha-keto acid. Above alpha-keto acid is alpha-ketoglutarate, which points down and around to glutamate. It also points down and around to glutamate, where –OOC bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH. CH bonds up to NH3 (plus sign above N), which bonds right to COO-. The glutamine molecule points down to glutamine, now in the mitochondrial matrix. Glutamine has an arrow pointing down, then right, represented as glutaminase (in blue), to glutamate. Glutamate in the mitochondrial matrix has an arrow pointing down to it from glutamate above the matrix. Below glutamate in the matrix is an arrow pointing down to NH4+ in a blue box, which has another arrow jetting right to alpha-keto-glutarate. There is a second arrow from glutamate pointing the same to form a type of box. In that box is glutamate dehydrogenase (in blue). To the right of this is a curved arrow, which begins with oxaloacetate, where –OOC bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to C, which double bonds up to O and bonds right to COO- all in red. This arrow is represented as aspartate aminotransferase (in blue) and points to aspartate, where –OOC bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH, which bonds right to COO- (all in a pink box). CH also bonds up to NH3 (plus sign above N, all in green box). Another arrow points down, then right from glutamine to NH4+ in a blue box. This has an arrow pointing down to carbamoyl phosphate, represented as carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 (in blue). To the left of the arrow, there are two curved arrows. The first begins with HCO3- (C is highlighted yellow) and the second begins with 2 ATP (ATP is in an orange oval). They both point to 2ADP [plus] Pi. Carbamoyl phosphate begins with C (highlighted in yellow), which bonds left to H2N (in a blue box), double bonds up to O, and bonds right to O, which bonds right to P, which double bonds up to O and bonds down and right to O-. Carbamoyl phosphate points to Pi with a curved blue arrow. This is step 1. Below this begins the urea cycle, which is circular with blue arrows. To the left, still in the mitochondrial matrix but part of the urea cycle, is ornithine. This begins with H3N (plus sign over N), which bonds right to (CH2)3, which bonds right to CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N) and bonds right to COO-. Ornithine points to citrulline with a cured blue arrow, represented as ornithine transcarbamoylase (in blue). Citrulline begins with C (highlighted in yellow), which bonds left to H2N (in a blue box), double bonds up to O, and bonds right to NH, which bonds right to (CH2)3, which bonds right to CH, up to NH3 (plus sign over N), and right to COO-. This points down and around to citrulline in the cytosol box, which points down and around to citrullyl-AMP intermediate in brackets. This arrow is identified as argininosuccinate synthetase (in blue). To the right is a curved blue arrow that points from ATP in an orange oval to PPi. This is step 2a. Citrullyl-AMP intermediate begins with C (highlighted in yellow), which double bonds left to HN (in a blue box), bonds right to NH, which bonds right to (CH2)3, which bonds right to CH. CH bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N), which bonds right to COO-. The yellow highlighted C also bonds down to O, which bonds down to P. P double bonds left to O, right to O-, and down to O, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to H, which is the left point of a pentagon. The top point is O, the right point has N bonding down to H. N is the bottom left point of a pentagon. N is also on the top of the pentagon. There is a double-side on the top left and right sides. The right side is shared in a hexagon to the right. The top point bonds up to NH2. N is at the right top and bottom points. The top right and bottom right sides are double-bonded. In the first pentagon, H (inside the pentagon) bonds down to OH on the bottom right point. H (inside pentagon) bonds down to OH on the bottom left point. The three bottom sides all have thick sides. Below this is a blue arrow pointing to argininosuccinate. To the right of the arrow has aspartate pointing to AMP, which is step 2b. Aspartate begins with –OOC, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds to CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign on top of N) in a green box, which bonds right to COO-. This is all in a pink box. Aspartate, as discussed earlier, also has an arrow pointing right and down to this molecule. Argininosuccinate begins with –OOC, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH, which bonds up to COO- (all in a pink box), and right to NH (in a green box). NH bonds right to C (highlighted in yellow), which double bonds up to NH2 (plus sign above N) in a blue box. C also bonds right to NH, which bonds right to (CH2)3, which bonds right to CH. CH bonds up to NH3 (plus sign above N), which bonds right to COO-. This has a blue arrow pointing to arginine on the circle and another arrow pointing off to fumarate. Fumarate begins with –OOC, which bonds right to CH, which double bonds right to CH, which bonds right to COO-. Arginine begins with C (Highlighted in yellow) bonds left to H2N (in green box), double bonds up to NH2 (plus sign above N), and bonds right to NH, which bonds right to (CH2)3, which bonds to CH. CH bonds up to NH3 (plus sign above N), and right to COO-. Arginine has a blue arrow up and around to ornithine. This arrow is identified as arginase (in blue). To the left of the arrow H20 points to urea with a cured arrow. Urea begins with C (highlighted in yellow), which bonds left to H2N (in a green box), double bonds up to O, and bonds right to NH2 (in a blue box). Ornithine begins with H3N (plus sign over N), which bonds right to (CH2)3, which bonds right to CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign above N), and right to COO-. This has an arrow leading back and up to ornithine in the mitochondrial matrix.
